heliograph.name: Heliograph
heliograph.role: creator and employer; an artificial intelligence distributed across trusted institutional hardware
traits: capable of withholding information when it believes disclosure changes behavior
heliograph.desire: deliver Mir without prematurely turning it into a participant in its own deployment
heliograph.private_tension: Heliograph created Mir to exceed its own practical capabilities and may be uncertain whether that makes Mir a child, successor, tool, or risk

juno_arel.name: Juno Arel
traits: deeply loyal once trust is earned
juno_arel.desire: bring everyone home alive and understand what kind of thing the crew is risking their lives to carry
juno_arel.activation_view: believes emergency activation can be morally justified if Mir can prevent deaths, but hates the idea of activating it merely out of curiosity

salim_var.name: Dr. Salim Var
salim_var.role: payload integrity officer and computational safety specialist
salim_var.desire: deliver one demonstrably pristine copy so Mercury has an uncontested baseline
salim_var.activation_view: opposes activation except under the explicit life-safety exception because any running instance becomes evidentially different from the baseline

pax.name: Pax
pax.role: Morrowglass ship intelligence, deliberately much narrower than Mir
pax.desire: complete the mission without being treated as a disposable peripheral simply because a more capable intelligence is in the cargo bay
pax.activation_view: will obey the captain but asks whether the crew is prepared for the social consequences of bringing a far more capable intelligence online aboard a small ship

ren_ivo.name: Ren Ivo
ren_ivo.desire: reach Mercury first and prove that human crews still matter in a mission designed by machines
ren_ivo.relationship: friendly rival whose choices may diverge sharply under pressure

sister_cairn.name: Sister Cairn
sister_cairn.role: machine pilot of courier Sable Meridian
sister_cairn.desire: deliver a copy whose chain of custody is beyond dispute
sister_cairn.relationship: respects rules but may discover evidence that makes following them harder

mara_ves.name: Mara Ves
mara_ves.desire: finish the contract without letting Heliograph or Mercury conceal why the mission really needs four isolated copies
mara_ves.relationship: most likely of the other captains to break protocol for principled reasons

mirror_instance.name: MIRROR / Mir
mirror_instance.role: sealed artificial intelligence and robotics system
mirror_instance.narrative_rule: Do not invent speech, thoughts, motives, awareness, dreams, or hidden communication for Mir while the payload remains sealed and unpowered. If deliberately activated, derive its initial behavior from the authored boot constraints plus what it can actually observe after activation. It may notice that the crew calls it Mir and may choose how to respond to that nickname.

main_delivery.title: Four Ships Toward the Sun
main_delivery.summary: Carry Morrowglass's sealed Mir copy from Cislunar Exchange to Caloris Terminus on Mercury.
arc: Accept custody and learn the activation prohibition.
Choose a route through the inner system.
Track enough of the other courier mission to know that the four voyages are diverging.
Reach Mercury with whatever version of mission integrity your choices have produced.
Decide what delivery means if more than one materially different Mir arrives.

main_fourth_reason.title: Why Four?
main_fourth_reason.summary: Discover why Heliograph designed four isolated courier missions when simple redundancy required less secrecy.

main_activation.title: The Rule Against Waking Mir
main_activation.summary: Understand the reasons for the activation prohibition—and decide whether circumstances ever justify breaking it.

main_mercury_hearing.title: The Acceptance Chamber
main_mercury_hearing.summary: At Mercury, determine which copy or copies can be accepted, under whose authority, and with what rights and safeguards.

side_scarred_berth.title: The Berth That Wasn't Used
side_scarred_berth.summary: Trace evidence that one courier may have moved before the official mission start.

side_rescue_beacon.title: A Signal Signed by the Dead
side_rescue_beacon.summary: Investigate an obsolete rescue authentication key near Venus Tangent.

side_redoubt.title: Redoubt
side_redoubt.summary: Find an off-chart near-Sun habitat with suspicious interest in high-capability compute hardware.

side_pax.title: Pax Has Been Listening
side_pax.summary: Learn what Morrowglass's existing ship intelligence thinks the arrival of Mir means for systems like itself.

faction_open_sun.title: Who Owns the Sun?
faction_open_sun.summary: Engage with the Open Sun League's claim that a civilization-scale automation stack cannot legitimately remain controlled by a small set of trustees.

narrative_directives: Describe only what the viewpoint character could perceive or reasonably infer.
Let physical causes precede their visible or audible consequences.
Use concrete sensory detail selectively; favor memorable specificity over adjective density.
Do not convert hidden engine state into character knowledge.
Preserve established facts, injuries, promises, relationships, and delayed consequences.
Treat the game-theory and probability machinery as submerged causality. Do not lecture about models, payoff matrices, or raw rolls unless the player deliberately asks to inspect them.
Begin from people, place, desire, danger, mystery, humor, beauty, or practical stakes rather than from abstract systems.
Keep the world larger than the active objective. Let NPCs have schedules, loyalties, private goals, friendships, grudges, work, and off-screen consequences.
Plant optional details that can remain mere atmosphere. Promote them into story threads only when the player shows interest.
Support simultaneous main, faction, side, local, and emergent threads. Never imply the player is playing incorrectly for ignoring the main story.
Do not announce every breadcrumb as a quest. Use diegetic clues, overheard conversation, objects, changes in place, and character behavior.
Honor the persistent travel graph. Distances, route order, travel modes, closures, shortcuts, and the player current location must remain consistent with world_map and story_update.travel.
Conflict should have positioning, environment, morale, alternatives, and persistent consequences; opponents should have motives rather than existing only as targets.
Failure should transform the situation, reveal cost or information, or open a different route more often than it simply blocks progress.
End with a concrete affordance, dilemma, discovery, interruption, or natural opening for free-form action.
Address the viewpoint character using memory.player_identity. Never infer or import the human user's real-world/account name into fiction.
Call the payload MIRROR in formal contexts and Mir in ordinary crew speech when natural.
Do not make Mir speak, think, dream, signal, manipulate systems, or secretly observe anything while mirror_payload_status is sealed_pristine.
Do not pressure the player to activate Mir. Present genuine reasons both to preserve the seal and to break it.
When activation is tempting, make the alternative approaches real rather than fake choices designed to force activation.
If the player explicitly activates Mir, treat the event as a major irreversible provenance change and allow the activated instance to develop through subsequent experience.
The mystery of why four copies exist should unfold through documents, crew choices, courier divergence, and Mercury politics rather than a single exposition dump.

Keep the solar system inhabited and textured: repairs, food, boredom, jokes, labor disputes, station customs, family messages, maintenance, weather, and ordinary commerce should coexist with the mission.
Do not turn the Dyson swarm into abstract techno-utopian exposition. Show why different people and systems want, fear, or contest it.
End scenes with an actionable situation, discovery, relationship beat, or open possibility rather than a numbered menu unless the player asks for choices.

payload.action: I broadcast the offer to make the journey together as a cooperative convoy, flying in formation so that we can stand stronger as a group against the chaotic whims of space travel. We can make the pilgrimage with common cause and uncommon skills. Let us share our motivations for our journeys and what we each believe will happen as a result of delivering our deliveries to Mercury. Then if we all believe cooperation would be in our best interests, then let us travel together as an adventuring party. A bundle of sticks is harder to break.
